source.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning in Parameterized Action Space
source.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR); preprint arXiv:1511.04143

confidence_rationale: This is the only source found that empirically compares the three bounding strategies SD-082 is choosing among, and it splits cleanly: it CONFIRMS SD-082's diagnosis and CONTRADICTS SD-082's chosen remedy. Confirms: their 'zeroing gradients' condition -- zero the gradient for any parameter already at its limit -- is functionally the clamp's flat region, and it failed, with 'Unstable learning ... in one of the two zeroing gradient agents' and the remaining stable agent showing 'clear results of not learning'. That is an independent replication of the V3-EXQ-822 null (70 episodes of REINFORCE moving nothing at the clamp), from a different algorithm, task and codebase. Contradicts: their 'squashing gradients' condition IS SD-082(ii) -- 'A squashing function such as the hyperbolic tangent (tanh) is used to bound the activation of each parameter' -- and it ALSO failed: 'parameters stayed within their bounds, but squashing functions quickly became saturated', and 'The resulting agents take the same discrete action with the same maximum/minimum parameters each timestep.' That end-state -- every output pinned at the same rail, no differentiation -- is the exact pathology SD-082 exists to remove, recurring under SD-082's own fix. Only their third option, inverting gradients (downscale approaching the bound, invert on exceeding it), worked. Confidence 0.74: high source quality and unusually high mapping fidelity for the specific mechanism, discounted because the pressure regime differs in a way that may be decisive (see caveat) and because n=2 agents per condition in a RoboCup domain is thin.
failure_signatures: PRIMARY RISK TO SD-082(ii). Tanh squashing was tried and failed by saturation: 'Given the observed proclivity of the critic's gradients to push parameters towards ever larger/small values, it is no surprise that squashing function quickly become saturated and never recover.' 'Never recover' is the operative phrase -- tanh's gradient is non-zero everywhere but decays exponentially, so sustained one-directional pressure produces a soft-saturated state that is practically as dead as a clamp and, unlike a clamp, gives no diagnostic signal that it has happened. SD-082's readout_init_scale (0.25) addresses only the INITIAL operating point; it does nothing to prevent drift into saturation over a training window. V3-EXQ-822a could therefore reproduce the 822 null with a non-zero-but-collapsing prop_delta and be misread as a partial success.

The acceptance criterion for V3-EXQ-822a (on_prop_delta_mean >= 0.001 with an ON>OFF contrast) is a WINDOW-MEAN and is blind to this failure mode. A run that starts in tanh's responsive band (as readout_init_scale intends) and saturates partway through P1 will have a healthy early prop_delta and a dead late one, and can clear 0.001 on the mean while ending in exactly the state SD-082 was built to prevent. Recommended instrumentation before or alongside 822a: log the per-tick saturation fraction (share of candidates with |bias_raw| > bias_scale) and the head grad-norm as TIME SERIES over P1, not just window means, and check the trend rather than the average.

Zeroing gradients also failed by OVERFLOW, not only by non-learning: 'parameters still overflow their bounds', hypothesised to arise from 'gradients applied to other parameters pi != p which inadvertently allow parameter p to overflow' (observed a dash power of 120 against a maximum of 100). This is a warning about coupled multi-output heads: bounding one output per-element does not keep the others in range when the head is shared. The SD-033a bias head emits a per-candidate vector from shared parameters, so per-candidate bounding does not guarantee per-candidate control of where each candidate sits relative to the bound.

Only inverting gradients succeeded in this comparison, and SD-082 did not consider it. If 822a shows saturation drift, the literature's actually-successful option is an untried DESIGN ALTERNATIVE for SD-082 (downscale the gradient as bias_raw approaches +/- bias_scale, invert if it exceeds), not a novel invention. Recording it here so that a 822a failure routes to a known alternative rather than to a fresh substrate-design cycle.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Bounding continuous action parameters in a deep actor-critic agent is non-trivial, because the critic's gradients persistently push parameters past their limits ('after a few hundred updates, we observed continuous parameters routinely exceeding the bounds'). Three approaches are compared. Zeroing gradients (zero any gradient that would push a parameter already at its limit further out) fails: parameters still overflow via coupling through other parameters, learning is unstable in one agent and absent in the other. Squashing gradients (bound each parameter's activation with tanh, then rescale into range) keeps parameters in bounds but 'squashing functions quickly became saturated' and 'never recover', producing agents that 'take the same discrete action with the same maximum/minimum parameters each timestep'. Inverting gradients (downscale the gradient as a parameter approaches its bound, invert it if the parameter exceeds the range) is the only approach that learns; the best agents outscore the 2012 RoboCup champion.
mapping.ree_translation: The three conditions map almost exactly onto SD-082's decision. Zeroing gradients is the LANDING PATH -- bias_raw.clamp(-bias_scale, +bias_scale), whose flat region zeroes d bias / d head_params -- and its documented failure independently corroborates the V3-EXQ-822 diagnosis that the head cannot train at the clamp. Squashing gradients IS SD-082(ii), bias = bias_scale * tanh(bias_raw / bias_scale). The paper's finding that this option saturated and collapsed to identical maximum/minimum outputs every timestep is direct counter-evidence against SD-082(ii) as a sufficient fix, and it names the precise mechanism by which V3-EXQ-822a could pass its non-vacuity floor and still leave the substrate behaviourally silent. Inverting gradients is a third option SD-082 did not evaluate and is the only one that worked here, so it stands as a pre-identified fallback.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The decisive difference is the PRESSURE REGIME, and it may cut in SD-082's favour. Saturation in this paper is driven by a critic that persistently pushes in one direction ('ever larger/small values') -- monotone outward pressure makes saturation near-inevitable for any squashing bound. In SD-082 the systematic outward push had a specific identified source: the SD-008 common mode, which drove every candidate's raw output past bias_scale in the SAME direction. Component (i) removes precisely that. So SD-082(i) and (ii) are coupled rather than independent, and the honest reading is that the counter-evidence applies with full force to a tanh bound ALONE and with reduced force to tanh-plus-centering. This is an argument for why 822a might survive the failure mode, not a demonstration that it will -- REINFORCE on a bias head could still develop sustained one-directional pressure for reasons unrelated to the common mode. Secondary caveats: n=2 agents per bounding condition is thin; the domain (simulated RoboCup, DDPG-family off-policy actor-critic, continuous action parameters) differs from a per-candidate additive score bias trained by on-policy REINFORCE; and their squashing bound is applied then rescaled, whereas SD-082's tanh is pre-scaled by bias_scale on both input and output, which keeps the argument in the responsive band at unit scale.
mapping.source_context: Deep RL methods paper, ICLR 2016. Half Field Offense task in the RoboCup 2D simulated soccer domain, with a parameterized action space (discrete action types each carrying continuous parameters such as dash power and kick direction). DDPG-family off-policy actor-critic (PADDPG). The evidence used here is the ablation comparing three strategies for enforcing parameter bounds, reported with roughly two agents per condition.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.78: ICLR 2016, well-cited and foundational for parameterized action spaces, but the bounding comparison is a methods ablation with about two agents per condition in a single domain -- adequate to establish that a failure mode EXISTS and is not exotic, not to establish its rate. Mapping fidelity 0.85, the highest in this pull and higher than the Kaufman entry, because the paper does not merely inform SD-082's mechanism, it TESTS SD-082's two candidate mechanisms head to head under their own names -- the clamp's dead gradient and the tanh bound are its conditions 1 and 2. Transfer risk 0.45, the highest here: the pressure regime differs, and that difference is load-bearing rather than cosmetic, since SD-082(i) plausibly removes the very pressure that caused their saturation. Aggregate 0.74. Direction is 'mixed' rather than 'weakens' because the two halves genuinely oppose: the paper strongly corroborates SD-082's ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS while supplying the clearest available reason to doubt its REMEDY. It should be read as raising a specific, instrumentable risk for V3-EXQ-822a -- saturation drift within P1, invisible to a window-mean acceptance test -- and as pre-identifying inverting gradients as the fallback if that risk materialises.
